recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-31687 unless Patient Care opens a new tracker to revise broader Condition date semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-31687 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 by Patient Care. It requested comments on both Condition.onset[x] and Condition.abatement[x] explaining that Condition.code can represent different granularities over time, making onset and abatement dates ambiguous as to whether they apply to the current code or an earlier representation.
initial_application: The Jira-linked commit fae49f4994c73b7ac34fc53bde6373fa50928ab4 added the requested ambiguity sentence and severe asthma example to both Condition.onset[x] and Condition.abatement[x] comments. Git pickaxe searches for the exact requested phrase found that commit as the source introduction.
additional_context: Condition is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. FHIR-25123 supplied recurrence/relapse examples that exposed the ambiguity, but it was separately Resolved - No Change. Later Condition comment edits, including J#42978 for onset and J#50437 for abatement, preserved the FHIR-31687 language while adding adjacent guidance. Confluence minutes align with the Jira record, and Zulip searches found no direct FHIR-31687 discussion or conflicting core Condition onset/abatement rationale.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk was needed because source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml already has the requested ambiguity text on both affected elements.
